issue_request: FHIR-11423 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2. The ballot comment proposed adding Coding to Request.occurrence[x] to represent STAT/high/low priority, but the accepted resolution said coded timings were already supported in Timing and directed adding a separate Request.priority element to the Request pattern.
initial_application: Commit 839bf586d6c1cf9a322e122852f0cc49bcfed263, a workflow commit explicitly listing #11423, added Request.priority 0..1 as a coded RequestPriority element with routine, urgent, asap, and stat codes and left Request.occurrence[x] as dateTime|Period|Timing.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists request under active logical patterns, so source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml is build-scope source for the current Request pattern. Current source still has Request.priority as a code bound to the request-priority terminology and keeps occurrence[x] limited to dateTime, Period, and Timing. Later FHIR-55655 discusses Request.priority binding strictness, but it is Resolved - change required and outside this default applied/published reconciliation scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys the implemented FHIR-11423 rule that priority is represented by Request.priority rather than by adding Coding to occurrence[x]. Changing Request.priority to CodeableConcept here would be broader than the historical #11423 application and would overlap later binding discussions that need separate handling.
